deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous folio): Riemann is finding the minimal surfaces foliated by circles lying in the parallel planes x = const. This is the problem behind his posthumous memoir on minimal surfaces (ed. Hattendorff, 1867), which treats surfaces bounded by two circles in parallel planes.

Setup carried over from the previous folio:
- The circle in the plane x has centre (x, -alpha, -beta) and radius^2 = -q.
- The minimal-surface condition reduces to the ODE q q'' - q'^2 + 2q + 2k q^3 = 0, where k = a^2 + b^2.
- With p = q' (so q'' = p dp/dq), the ODE becomes linear in u = p^2: (q/2) du/dq - u = -2q - 2k q^3.
- Hence (u/q^2)' = -4/q^2 - 4k, so u/q^2 = 4/q - 4kq + 8c.
- Therefore p = 2 sqrt(q(1 + 2cq - kq^2)).
- The parametrisation is then:
  - x = ∫ dq / (2 sqrt(q(1 + 2cq - kq^2))),
  - m = ∫ q dx = ∫ q dq / (2 sqrt(q(1 + 2cq - kq^2))),
  - alpha = -a m + d, beta = -b m + e,
  - y = a m - d + sqrt(-q) cos psi,
  - z = b m - e + sqrt(-q) sin psi.

This folio, step by step:
(1) Apart from algebraic terms (sqrt(-q) cos psi, sqrt(-q) sin psi and constants), the coordinates are elliptic integrals with upper limit q. The radicand q(1 + 2cq - kq^2) is a cubic in q, so the integrals are elliptic. x is an integral of the first kind; m, which contains q in the numerator, is of the second kind. The parenthetical, transcribed '(nur 4 unabhängige)', probably reads '(nur 1ter und 2ter Gattung)' — 'only of the first and second kind' — and that reading fits the mathematics exactly.
(2) By the general formulas developed earlier in the manuscript (Riemann's conformal representation of minimal surfaces), the coordinates X, Y, Z can be written as sums of two conjugate functions of two conjugate complex variables (eta, eta'). That is, x = F(eta) + conj F(eta), the analogue of the Weierstrass–Enneper representation, which Riemann had in his own form.
(3) Riemann conjectures that the elliptic-integral expressions in the real variable q can be recombined, via the addition theorems for elliptic integrals, into a single integral expression in the variable q. An integral at q then equals the sum of the integrals at two conjugate complex points, plus algebraic terms, which matches the conjugate-sum form.
(4) He states that this is easily confirmed, referring to a computation for Z further on, which is not on this page.

No explicit computation appears on this folio; it is a programmatic remark linking the explicit integration to the conformal representation.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.
The ODE solution on the preceding page checks out (verified below).
Claim (4) is asserted without proof here; it is deferred to 'Z unten', which is not on this folio.

results.what: Coordinates of the circle-foliated minimal surface expressed, up to algebraic terms, by elliptic integrals of the first and second kind with upper limit q
results.modern_name: Riemann minimal examples (Riemann's one-parameter family of periodic minimal surfaces foliated by circles/lines in parallel planes)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous memoir, Hattendorff 1867); Enneper (1869) also treated circle-foliated minimal surfaces

results.what: Matching the real elliptic-integral parametrisation with the conformal (Weierstrass-type) representation X = F(eta) + F'(eta') via the addition theorem for elliptic integrals
results.modern_name: Weierstrass–Enneper representation; Abel/Euler addition theorem for elliptic integrals
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass and Enneper (1863–66) for the representation; Euler/Abel/Legendre for the addition theorem; Riemann had his own version in the minimal-surface memoir

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working note behind Riemann's published posthumous treatment of minimal surfaces bounded by two circles in parallel planes. The elliptic-integral parametrisation and its link to the conformal representation are already known to be his (Hattendorff's 1867 edition). The page contains a conjecture and a check, not a new result.

checkable.asserts: p^2 = 4q(1+2cq-kq^2) solves the reduced first-order equation q p dp/dq - p^2 + 2q + 2kq^3 = 0 (k = a^2+b^2)
(p/q)^2 = 4/q - 4kq + 8c, as written on the previous page
The cubic radicand has nonzero discriminant 4(c^2+k) generically, so the integrals in q are genuinely elliptic
dm/dx = q, consistent with m = ∫ q dx and the two integrands dx/dq = 1/(2R), dm/dq = q/(2R)

transcription_corrections: '(nur 4 unabhängige)' most likely reads '(nur 1ter und 2ter Gattung)', i.e. elliptic integrals only of the first and second kind; this fits x (first kind) and m (second kind).

'Summen von (einer) eingesetzten Functionen gewisser eingesetzter Veränderlichen' should very probably read 'Summen von zwei conjugirten Functionen zweier conjugirter Veränderlichen' (Riemann's standard phrasing for the conformal representation with conjugate variables eta, eta').
'zusammenfassen lassen lassen' contains a duplicated 'lassen' (dittography in the transcription, or a line-break repetition).
